newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-MONACO REACH UEFA CUP LAST EIGHT FOR FIRST TIME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MONACO REACH UEFA CUP LAST EIGHT FOR FIRST TIME.

text.p: Monaco swept into the quarter-finals of the UEFA Cup for the first time in their history on Tuesday, beating Germany's Hamburg 2-0 in their third round second leg to seal a 5-0 aggregate victory.

Hamburg, 3-0 down after the first leg, made most of the running for the first hour but then Monaco's Victor Ikpeba received a perfect pass from Ali Benarbia after 62 minutes and Hamburg goalkeeper Richard Golz failed to hold the Nigerian striker's shot.
Benarbia scored the second two minutes from the end from the penalty spot after Bosnian Hasan Salihamidzic was sent off for a last-ditch foul aimed at preventing a goal.
Hamburg, hampered by the suspension of midfielder Markus Schupp, were the second German club eliminated from the UEFA Cup on Tuesday after Karlsruhe were beaten 5-0 on the night by Denmark's Brondby.
Hamburg began in determined fashion and Karsten Baeron forced Monaco goalkeeper Fabien Barthez to make two difficult saves in the first nine minutes.
Barthez went on to make a brilliant save from a header by Salihamidzic in the 29th minute as Hamburg maintained the pressure.
